full_name: International Network for Advanced AI Measurement, Evaluation and Science (formerly International Network of AI Safety Institutes)
mission: A club of government AI evaluation bodies from Australia, Canada, the EU, France, Japan, Kenya, Korea, Singapore, the UK and the US. Members agree shared practices for measuring and testing advanced AI so that results are comparable across borders and languages, and run joint testing exercises.

key_work.title: Network Best Practice: Automated Evaluation of Large Language Models
key_work.plain_summary: A shared rulebook for running automated LLM evaluations well (design, reporting, reproducibility), agreed at the Seoul meeting in July 2026.

key_work.title: Consensus Areas on Practices for Automated Evaluations
key_work.plain_summary: The network's first list of agreed practices and open questions for automated AI evaluations (Feb 2026).

key_work.title: Renaming announcement (UK government press release)
key_work.plain_summary: Explains the Dec 2025 re-focus on measurement and evaluation science and the UK's new coordinator role.

status_note: announced at the AI Seoul Summit (May 2024), first convened Nov 2024 in San Francisco as the International Network of AI Safety Institutes; renamed in Dec 2025 (dropping 'safety') with the UK AISI as network coordinator. Met in San Diego (Dec 2025), Hiroshima forum (Jan 2026) and Seoul (2026).

funding_note: No central budget; each member funds its own institute.
size_note: 10 members (Australia, Canada, EU, France, Japan, Kenya, Korea, Singapore, UK, US).
events: International Network of AI Safety Institutes renamed, dropping “safety”

people.role: Network representative for Korea (Korea AISI Director)

warnings.text: Without shared evaluation methods, results from different countries cannot be compared or trusted.
AI behaves differently across languages and cultures, so single-country testing misses failures.

recommendations.text: Adopt common, documented best practices for automated evaluations.
Run joint and multilingual testing across member institutes.
